description: Single-panel engineering stress–strain plot labelled "(c)" in the top-left corner, one panel of the Fe30MnxAl1C (1050 °C) series; no caption was supplied. The abscissa is ε_E, engineering strain in % (0–80, ticks every 20 %); the ordinate is σ_E, engineering stress in MPa (0–1500, gridlines every 300 MPa). An inset legend identifies five solid curves: 6Al (black), 8Al (red), 10Al (green), 11Al (blue) and 12Al (cyan). Every curve rises linearly, then strain-hardens toward the 800–900 MPa region before a rapid load drop at failure. Increasing Al raises the flow stress and shortens elongation: 6Al starts lowest (between the 300 and 600 MPa gridlines) and is the last to fail (~70 % strain); 8Al (starting in the 500–600 MPa band) and 10Al (600–700 MPa) lie systematically higher; 11Al starts near 700 MPa, quickly plateaus between the 600 and 900 MPa gridlines and then drops steeply around 62 %; 12Al starts highest (just above 900 MPa), holds an almost flat yield plateau and fails abruptly at roughly 45 % strain — the lowest ductility. The panel demonstrates the strength–ductility trade-off with increasing Al in these low-density steels.

observations.observation: Panel (c) plots engineering stress σ_E (MPa, 0–1500, gridlines every 300 MPa) against engineering strain ε_E (%, 0–80, ticks every 20 %).
The legend names the alloy condition 'Fe30MnxAl1C (1050°C)' and contains five curves: 6Al (black), 8Al (red), 10Al (green), 11Al (blue), 12Al (cyan).
The 12Al (cyan) curve has the highest initial stress (just above the 900 MPa gridline) and displays an almost flat yield plateau rather than a pronounced hardening stage.

The 6Al (black) curve starts lowest, between the 300 and 600 MPa gridlines, and is still rising when the other curves have already fractured, failing at the largest strain of the set (near the 70 % region of the axis).
Curve ordering at low strain is monotonic in Al content: 6Al < 8Al < 10Al < 11Al < 12Al in flow stress.
The 12Al curve fails abruptly at approximately 45 % strain, the earliest failure among the five curves, whereas 6Al, 8Al and 10Al extend to about 65–72 % strain.

All five curves reach a maximum between the 800 and 900 MPa gridlines before the terminal load drop, so the tensile strength differences between compositions are small compared with the differences in elongation.
No numeric value labels are printed on the curves themselves; only axis ticks and the legend text carry printed values.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress–strain curves (σ_E in MPa vs ε_E in %) for Fe30MnxAl1C (1050 °C) with five legend-labelled curves: 6Al, 8Al, 10Al, 11Al and 12Al. All curves show yield, strain hardening to a maximum near the 800–900 MPa gridlines, and abrupt fracture; the highest-Al (12Al) curve has the highest yield/plateau stress and fails earliest (~45 % strain), while 6Al has the lowest strength and the largest elongation.
